chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) walked behind a coffin, so it was said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, why do you walk behind it?' He said, 'The angels, I see them walking in front of it, and we are following them.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet walk behind the coffin instead of in front?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) observance of the unseen spiritual hierarchy, where he followed the angels leading the deceased, thereby establishing the sunnah of walking behind the coffin as an act of humility and reverence. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a demonstration of the Prophet’s adherence to divine order and his role in modeling proper etiquette for the community during the transition of the soul. The practice underscores the belief that funeral rites are not merely social obligations but spiritual acts aligned with the movements of the celestial beings.
